decisive_items: symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection 3 days prior
low QRS voltage in limb leads
ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF, and V1-V6
response.rationale: Viral prodrome, diffuse ST elevation with low QRS voltage, severe LV dysfunction, and normal coronary arteries in a young patient are classic for fulminant myocarditis; sepsis, stress cardiomyopathy, and ACS do not explain the full ECG and cardiac pattern.

rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries and diffuse ST elevation/low voltage argue against acute coronary syndrome despite elevated troponin.
No precipitating stressor; infectious prodrome and diffuse ECG changes favor myocarditis over stress cardiomyopathy.
High procalcitonin and shock could suggest sepsis, but severe LV dysfunction with diffuse ST elevation/low voltage and normal coronaries is better explained by myocarditis.
